# Memory Principles {.unnumbered}

Part II analyzes the context memory hierarchy of agentic machine learning systems. We treat the active context window as an L1 attention working set subject to quadratic prefill complexity and physical HBM walls, develop L2 virtual context memory through PagedAttention and Radix-tree prefix sharing, and engineer L3 episodic trajectory storage through approximate nearest-neighbor vector indexes and relational knowledge graphs.

::: {#pri-vol3-attention-working-set .callout-principle title="Context as an L1 working set"}

**Invariant**: Context capacity is the L1 cache of neural compute: expressive, fast, strictly finite, and quadratically expensive in prefill compute ($O(C_i^2)$) and linear in HBM footprint.

**Implication**: Systems runtimes must actively manage context via eviction, prompt compaction, and selective attention to prevent Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) explosion and attention degradation.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-prefix-coherence .callout-principle title="Prefix locality and virtual memory paging"}

**Invariant**: Multi-turn agent trajectories exhibit massive prefix sharing; serving runtimes must exploit non-contiguous physical page allocation (PagedAttention) and Radix-tree KV reuse.

**Implication**: Schedulers must route multi-turn trajectories with session cache affinity, ensuring prompt templates prioritize static instructions to maximize hardware KV-cache reuse.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-episodic-storage-hierarchy .callout-principle title="The episodic storage hierarchy"}

**Invariant**: Working memory inside GPU HBM cannot scale to long-horizon history; scalable persistence requires an external L3 storage tier with explicit consolidation semantics.

**Implication**: Agent architectures must combine dense vector indexes (approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval) with symbolic relational graphs, bounded by strict retrieval SLA budgets.

:::
